描述_EN: amber, which was imported from burma or the baltic area, was a particularly rare material in china except during the liao (907–1115), yuan, and qing (1644–1911) dynasties, when nomadic imperial houses’ firm control of the central asian trade routes led to increased supplies. it provides evidence for the free flow of trade goods across the silk road as well as the contact between ancient china and other parts of the world. this carving of a dragon climbing across an ornamental garden rock exemplifies the richly articulated sculptural treatment of precious materials created during the yuan dynasty (1271–1368). the spirited dragon illustrates the continuation of the dynamic art of the tang dynasty (618–907) in northern china in the following centuries.
描述_ZN: 从缅甸或波罗的海地区进口的琥珀，在中国是一种特别罕见的材料，除了在辽（907-1115）、元和清（1644-1911）朝代，当时游牧民族的皇室对中亚贸易路线的牢固控制导致供应增加。 它为丝绸之路上贸易货物的自由流动以及古代中国与世界其他地区的联系提供了证据。 这幅龙爬过观赏性花园岩石的雕刻，体现了元代（1271-1368年）对珍贵材料的丰富的雕塑处理。 这条活泼的龙说明了唐代（618-907）的动态艺术在随后几个世纪在中国北方的延续。
